column3: The Hebrew repeats the high places as the location of sacrifice and burning incense; BSB uses there.
The Hebrew says the LORD struck the king and he became leprous until his death; BSB combines these clauses into afflicting him with leprosy until his death.
The Hebrew says they buried him with his fathers; BSB uses a passive and says near them.
The Hebrew says this was the word spoken to Jehu and adds that it happened so; BSB frames the sentence as fulfillment.
The Hebrew separately states going up and coming and repeats Samaria as the place of the attack; BSB condenses the movement and names Samaria once.
The Hebrew explicitly distinguishes everyone in Tiphsah from its surrounding territory; BSB combines them as everyone in its vicinity.
The Hebrew says all his days; BSB specifies throughout his reign.
The Hebrew uses the images of Pul’s hands being with Menahem and strengthening the kingdom in his hand; BSB expresses these as support and a stronger grip on the kingdom.
The Hebrew places Argob and Arieh after the description of the attack in the palace and separately says fifty Gileadites were with Pekah; BSB groups all of them as his fellow conspirators.
